messages:
maria gonzalez: Heads-up — seeing slow, steady memory growth from the KV cache on long-chat workloads (~12k-18k tokens). Not OOM yet but host RSS drifts up over hours. Profiling points to lots of tiny free fragments in the allocator (mostly 32-128B).

ajay singh: Can you paste the allocator stats dump? small sample is fine. wondering if it's freelist churn or fragmentation from mixed block sizes.

maria gonzalez: sure:```
kv_alloc_stats:
  total_allocs: 2.1M
  total_frees: 2.05M
  free_fragments: 42k
  avg_fragment_size: 96
  largest_free_run: 24KB
  active_kv_items: 48k
```
looks like a lot of leftover micro-blocks. Most KV entries are 600-2k bytes after serialization, but we keep allocating 64B slabs for the small tail.

kevin lee: that matches what I saw in the perf trace: many short-lived allocations pinned by the batching pipeline. Continuous-batching keeps KVs referenced longer which prevents coalescing. Could be exacerbated by the new kernel selection that holds longer per-request state for optimized attention.

sophie chan: idea: run a "mini-compaction" that coalesces adjacent free fragments into larger blocks when free_fragment_count > threshold, rather than waiting for a major compaction cycle. Low-latency friendly: do incremental and rate-limit CPU.

maria gonzalez: exactly — I prototyped a simple pass that scans 4x per-minute and merges neighbouring free runs up to 64KB. Results on a staging run: RSS slope flattened, 7% lower p50 allocation latency, but compaction CPU bumped ~3%.

ajay singh: can you share the prototype flags? also any regressed tail latencies? We need to avoid stop-the-world effects.

maria gonzalez: prototype flags: `kv.compact.enabled=1`, `kv.compact.rate=250ms`, `kv.compact.max_merge=65536`. No noticeable tail p99 in our 1h stress but we saw a 95p bump of ~5ms during compaction windows.

kevin lee: tradeoff seems reasonable. Another lever: tune block size buckets. If we increase base block size from 64->128 or 256 we reduce micro-fragmentation but increase internal waste for tiny KVs. Worth simulating with our trace sampler.

sophie chan: +1 on simulation. Also add a policy: only run aggressive merges when cpu_idle> X or qlen<Y. We have telemetry events for cpu_idle and can gate compaction.

maria gonzalez: logged an experiment in canary: run mini-compact + increase base block to 128 for 6h, compare RSS slope and token-tail latencies. I'll attach perf summaries to the canary ticket after the run.

perf-bot: experiment registered: exp-id=kv-mini-compact-20260505-1, canary group: 5% traffic, metrics: kv_rss_slope, kv_fragment_count, p99_token_latency.

ajay singh: one more note — kernel selection change last week swapped to an attention kernel that keeps KV refs during cache warmup. If the canary shows improvement, we should consider coordinating compaction with the kernel's warmup lifecycle so we don't compact while kernels are holding live refs.

kevin lee: I'll add a short patch to add a kernel-ready hook into the KV manager to pause aggressive merges while a kernel holds a reservation. Simple mutex with try-lock semantics so compaction is opportunistic.

maria gonzalez: sweet. I'll run the canary tonight and post results here. thanks all. :thumbsup:

sophie chan: TY! if results look good we can roll to Dedicated clusters and add a perf regression test for kv_fragment_count in CI.

kevin lee: ack.
